producer_report.summary:
Turned on `[landing] merge_via_rest = true` in athena.toml, with a reason comment above it. The config.rs test now checks the default on a stripped config and asserts this repository's config turns the merge on. I added one entry to the existing `### Changed` section in CHANGELOG.md.

Root cause: the test pinned the live repository setting (it asserted `REPO_CONFIG` lacks `[landing]`) instead of the default. It now takes the part of REPO_CONFIG before `[landing]`. Since `[landing]` is the last table in athena.toml, that is the config with the table stripped. The test asserts the default is off there, that an explicit true turns it on, and that an empty table is off. It also asserts the full repository config gives `merge_via_rest == true`.

Checks: fmt and clippy are clean. `cargo test --locked -p athena-data rest_merge` passes. The full `cargo test --locked` printed a very long compile log, which I could not read in full. I saw no error in the part I read, but I did not confirm every test result.

checks_run.note: Ran to completion with no error shown in the readable part of the output; the persisted output was too large to read in full, so per-test results are not confirmed.

open_issues: The reading's assumption that Unreleased had no `### Changed` heading was wrong; the existing heading was used instead.
mistakes: I first added a duplicate `### Changed` heading under Added/Fixed because I trusted the reading's assumption without checking. I removed it and moved the entry into the existing section.
learnings: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased already has a `### Changed` heading (after `### Fixed`), contrary to the reading's assumption, so the entry went at the top of that section.
`[landing]` is placed last in athena.toml so the test can strip it with split_once.
Heredocs are denied by the Bash hook, so use Edit for file appends.
